children: Nvidia
is partnering with Swedish autonomous truck maker Einride
as the company prepares to expand production to meet growing demand for driverless vehicles.
The chipmaker will provide the computing platform and artificial-intelligence tools underpinning Einride’s autonomous-driving systems, Einride
said on Monday. The companies are developing the next generation of Einride Driver on Nvidia’s
Hyperion platform.
Einride

currently operates hundreds of electric trucks for shipping customers across the United States, Europe, and the Middle East. The company expects demand to rise to between 1,500 and 2,000 vehicles by 2028, with about 80% of that demand potentially suitable for automation in the medium term.
“Building the next generation of the Einride Driver on the Nvidia
Hyperion platform will enable us to scale autonomous deployment across a freight network that’s already serving customers today,” Henrik Green, Einride’s chief technology officer, said.
Nvidia
Vice President of Automotive Rishi Dhall said autonomous trucking could improve safety and efficiency in global freight.
Einride
, founded in Stockholm in 2016, began trading on the Nasdaq this summer following a merger with blank-check company Legato Merger Corp. III that valued its equity at $1.35 billion before proceeds.
The company has customers including PepsiCo
, Carlsberg, and Heineken
. Its partnership with Nvidia
comes as autonomous trucking gains traction alongside self-driving passenger vehicles and autonomous equipment.
ENRD was trading around 6% higher premarket on Monday.

title: Nvidia backs Einride expansion of autonomous electric trucks
